newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to be mixed on Wednesday on possible local-led profit taking despite the psychological boost of the overnight rise on Wall Street, brokers said.
They said the rise in the Dow Jones could spark some foreign buying of blue chips but the volume would be limited.

"Any possible rally could be limited by profit-taking. After all, the index has made significant gains for the last two days. Some investors might take profits, especially since on Thursday the market will close for a holiday," one broker with a Hong Kong-based securities firm said.
The government announcement of the April consumer price index, which is scheduled for Wednesday, could also affect market sentiment, brokers said.
They said some counters such as blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia might attract further market attention following revived talk of a possible acquisition.
"Those old rumours are spreading again in the market that the bank will acquire another bank in order to boost its assets," one broker with a local firm said.
Lippo Group companies such as Lippo Securities and Lippo Life were also likely to reap some positive sentiment on market talk that the group planned to hold a road show soon, brokers said.

Retailer Multipolar, also a member of the Lippo Group, could attract buyers after news that Hari Darmawan -- founder of Matahari Putra Prima -- had bought an additional five percent stake in the firm and planned to add to his holding.
Reports that distribution firm Wicaksana Overseas was planning to expand to the pharmaceutical business by acquiring another company could also boost sentiment, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the index gained 6.82 points, or 1.04 percent, to 659.60 points.
Indonesia is currently in the second week of the campaign for the May 29 elections and there have no major reports of violence.
Market heavyweight Telkom continued making gains by rising 75 rupiah to 3,675 rupiah in modest volume.
"Telkom has staged a strong rebound in the past several days. I think more foreign funds have started entering the market which has helped big-caps like Telkom," another broker said.
The broker said reports of the country's healthy February trade surplus and a slight increase in the April consumer price index were likely to keep sentiment steady on big-caps.
Tin miner Timah fell 125 rupiah to 3,500 rupiah amid news of lower first quarter net profit and the fact that the fabled Busang gold deposit was a dud, brokers said.

The most active Multipolar rose 75 rupiah to 1,700 rupiah, with some 17 million shares traded after news that retail tycoon Hari Dharmawan had completed his plan to buy a five percent stake in the firm, taking his holding to 10 percent.
